A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Path Gradients after Flow Matching by the same authors. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable and support matching retained content against additions in v2.

before.justification: v1 reports original experiments on a Gaussian mixture, Lennard-Jones systems, and alanine dipeptide, including sampling efficiency, likelihood, and flow-trajectory analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds evaluation of path-gradient fine-tuning on unseen dipeptides, reported in Section 4.3 and Table 5.

M1.justification: FM pre-training, forward-KL path-gradient fine-tuning, and augmented-adjoint computation remain unchanged. The transferability experiment applies the existing procedure to pretrained TBG models. Expanded estimator explanations and architecture descriptions do not establish a method change.

E1.justification: v2 adds the 2AA dataset and evaluation on 16 unseen dipeptides using a model trained on 200 dipeptides at 310 K. This substantially extends coverage from individual molecular and particle systems to generalization across molecules. The original Gaussian-mixture, Lennard-Jones, and alanine tasks remain.

E2.justification: Appendix A.8 and Table 4 add maximum-likelihood training from Garcia Satorras et al. (2021) as an LJ13 comparator, reporting NLL -15.83 ± 0.07 and ESSq 39.78 ± 6.19%. The existing FM and PG comparison methods remain; the additional comparator is confined to this comparison.

E3.justification: The added transferability experiment introduces a separate protocol: 200 training trajectories, 100 validation and 100 test trajectories, evaluation on a selected 16 test dipeptides, and six days of A100 fine-tuning at learning rate 0.00001. Existing experiment settings remain documented as before; no revised metrics or reruns of those experiments are established.

E4.justification: Appendix A.9 and Figure 8 add energy-distribution diagnostics for LJ13, LJ55, and seven test dipeptides, examining whether fine-tuning brings generated energies closer to reference distributions. The existing FM-loss, trajectory-length, alanine conformation, bond-length, and memory-budget analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Tables 1–3 retain mean ± standard error over three runs, and Appendix A.7 retains the disclosure that one divergent run was discarded and repeated. No new seed information or uncertainty-estimation procedure is introduced. The new transferability table supplies point estimates without run counts or uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: Tables 4–5 add ML-comparison and transferability results. Table 5 reports average NLL changing from -100.73 to -100.93 and ESSq from 7.96% to 9.79% after PG; five dipeptides nevertheless have lower ESSq. Figure 1 also changes displayed KL values: FM 0.076 to 0.067, PG 0.010 to 0.021, and hybrid 0.003 to 0.001, without documented setting changes. Tables 1–3 retain their numerical results.

T1.justification: New Appendix A.11 develops ML and PG estimator expressions and variance arguments. It adds an explicit Gaussian/identity-flow counterexample and proof reporting nonzero FM gradient variance of 8/(ND) at the density optimum, with an extension to OT-FM through permutation invariance. This goes substantially beyond v1's existing KL transformation and adjoint equations.

C1.justification: The abstract and contribution list retain the hybrid-training, sampling-efficiency, and trajectory-preservation claims. The discussion removes v1's prediction that PG or related methods will become state of the art for Boltzmann Generators and scientific generative models, modestly narrowing the concluding claims.

C2.justification: Section 2.4 adds discussion of self-sampling's missing-mode risks and repeated force-evaluation costs. Appendix A.11 adds a Lipschitz-based explanation of when PG variance may be favorable and explicitly limits the FM variance argument to a toy setting. The original limitations remain, while the new broader-impact paragraph raises incomplete sampling from missing convergence guarantees.

D1.justification: v2 adds a project repository link, 2AA dataset access and trajectory details, and hardware, duration, and learning-rate information for transferability fine-tuning. Existing implementation details are largely retained. The reprinted Algorithm 2 also loses its explicit return statement, a small documentation regression.

R1.justification: Section 2.4 more explicitly distinguishes this work from Vaitl et al. (2022a,b), emphasizing target-sample forward-KL training and investigation of FM-trained flows. The bibliography additionally lists the published Papamakarios review already cited in preprint form; this is not a distinct new research contribution being incorporated.

P1.justification: Most existing prose and the main narrative remain intact. Local revisions clarify terminology and FM variants, expand the prior-work comparison, and reorganize the experiment overview into three scenarios. Transferability, broader impact, acknowledgements, and appendix subsections are added, with pseudocode and code-library sections reordered.

P2.justification: v2 adds Tables 4–5 and the nine-panel Figure 8. Figure 1 gains explicit time ticks and seconds and reorders its method panels. Existing floats are relocated, ESS table headers are standardized, and both algorithms are placed together. The overall layout and remaining displays are largely preserved.

improvement.justification: v2 strengthens the explanation of PG's advantages, adds an ML comparator and useful evidence on unseen molecules, and supplies a project-code link. The transferability evidence lacks uncertainty reporting and a matched-compute FM control, limiting its implications. Appendix A.2 also retains the now-contradictory statement that TBG is not used transferably. These additions provide a positive but limited overall gain beyond the unchanged controlled experiments.
